relevance_note: Case report of two women with adult-onset Alexander disease 'confirmed via glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) mutation analysis', each described individually (sex, age, signs, MRI).
method_note: Hand extraction, no table transcription (the paper has no tables). Labels: the paper's own headings 'Case 1' / 'Case 2' (also 'patient 2' once in the Discussion); spans quote the figure captions. No GFAP variant description is printed for either patient (only 'GFAP mutation analysis'), so each has one variant row with variant_original_string 'not reported'; zygosity, inheritance, pathogenicity not reported. 'Sporadic AOAD' in the Discussion was not used for inheritance (no parental testing stated). Ages: 37 (Case 1) and 61 (Case 2) are ages at presentation/initial MRI, with symptom durations of 6 and 4 years; follow-up MRIs were 2 and 3 years later and diagnosis followed the MRI, so no age at onset, last evaluation or diagnosis is stated as such; all recorded 'not reported'. Contradiction: Fig. 2 caption title says 'MRI of AOAD in a 67-year-old female' while the case text and panel A say 61-year-old with follow-up after 3 years. Negative SCA-1/2/3/6/7/17, SPG3A and SPG4 gene tests 'in either case' are differential-diagnosis tests, not phenotypes; not recorded as features. Normal arylsulfatase A, galactocerebrosidase and VLCFA 'in either patient' recorded as excluded abnormalities (D-27) with basis 'inferred from group statement'. Discussion sentence 'Spasticity and paresthesia were slightly improved following conservative management' is about 'our patients' without saying which patient; treatment_summary left 'not reported' for both. Pial FLAIR rim along the brainstem surface (Case 1) was not treated as the checklist 'periventricular rim'. Spastic paraparesis (Case 1) and hemiparesis (Case 2) counted as limb weakness. Case 2's dizziness was not counted as ataxia; dentate nucleus signal is imaging only, not a cerebellar sign. Pial signal changes excluded for Case 2 from the Discussion sentence naming 'the second 61-year-old patient'. is_proband left null: two unrelated patients, neither called proband.
